questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

You will never get sufficient nourishment if you are __obdurate__ in refusing to eat vegetables.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (obedient). 'Obdurate' means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion. The antonym is obedient.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

Don't be so __obtrusive__ but instead, mind your own business.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (reserved). 'Obtrusive' means noticeable or prominent in an unwelcome way; intruding. The antonym is reserved.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

I admire people who are modest despite their __opulence__.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (poverty). 'Opulence' means great wealth. The antonym is poverty.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

Do you always try to be a __paragon__ of virtue?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (anomaly). A 'paragon' is a perfect example. The antonym is anomaly (something that deviates from the norm).

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

Tragic stories had so much __pathos__ that it left me feeling down.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (humor). 'Pathos' is a quality that evokes pity or sadness. The antonym is humor.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

Chin is such a __precocious__ girl who can already read at age three.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (slow learner). 'Precocious' means developing abilities early. The antonym is slow learner.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

She had the __quixotic__ idea that she was a reincarnation of a British princess.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (realistic). 'Quixotic' means exceedingly idealistic, unrealistic. The antonym is realistic.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

The __ramshackle__ building collapsed easily.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (new). 'Ramshackle' means in a state of severe disrepair. The antonym is new.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

An A-rating represents the __ultimate__ honor a film will ever have.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (least). 'Ultimate' means final or greatest. The antonym is least.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

CJ de Silva's painting abilities are __uncanny__.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (ordinary). 'Uncanny' means strange or mysterious, especially in an unsettling way; extraordinary. The antonym is ordinary.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

Lea Salonga's performance was __utterly__ delightful.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (somewhat). 'Utterly' means completely and absolutely. The antonym is somewhat.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

The strong current of the floodwaters caused the wooden bridge to __vacillate__.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (be firm). 'Vacillate' means to waver or be unsteady. The antonym is be firm.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

The __vindictive__ politician spread rumors about his opponent.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (forgiving). 'Vindictive' means having a strong desire for revenge. The antonym is forgiving.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

If words were swords, then her __vitriolic__ remarks could really kill.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (kind). 'Vitriolic' means filled with bitter criticism or malice. The antonym is kind.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

Many students __vouch for__ the effectiveness of the MSA Review classes.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (refute). 'Vouch for' means to assert or confirm the truth of something. The antonym is refute (disprove).

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

That __yonder__ youth is more studious than the nearer one.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (closer). 'Yonder' means at some distance. The antonym is closer.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

MSA tutors are all __zealous__ tutors who nourish eager minds.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (indifferent). 'Zealous' means having great energy or enthusiasm. The antonym is indifferent.

questions.question:
Choose the antonym of the underlined word.

Don't let __trivial__ things upset you.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (important). 'Trivial' means of little value or importance. The antonym is important.

questions.question: Mary Dick : Herman Melville :: The Old Man and the Sea : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (Ernest Hemingway). 'Moby Dick' was written by Herman Melville. 'The Old Man and the Sea' was written by Ernest Hemingway.

questions.question: Confucius : China :: Mahatma Gandhi : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (India). Confucius is associated with China. Mahatma Gandhi is associated with India.

questions.question: BIR : Taxes :: DPWH : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (Public Roads). BIR (Bureau of Internal Revenue) handles taxes. DPWH (Department of Public Works and Highways) handles public roads.

questions.question: Barangay : Captain :: Provincial Government : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (Governor). The head of a barangay is the barangay captain. The head of a provincial government is the governor.

questions.question: USA : Washington D.C. :: Philippines : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (Manila). The capital of the USA is Washington D.C. The capital of the Philippines is Manila.

questions.question: Presidential : President :: Parliamentary : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (Prime Minister). In a presidential system, the head is the President. In a parliamentary system, the head is the Prime Minister.

questions.question: Tagbanua : Palawan :: Kankanay : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (Benguet). The Tagbanua are an indigenous group from Palawan. The Kankanay are from Benguet.

questions.question: Pyramid : Egypt :: Taj Mahal : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (India). The Pyramids are in Egypt. The Taj Mahal is in India.

questions.question: Tigris-Euphrates : Mesopotamia :: Nile River : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (Egypt). The Tigris-Euphrates river system is associated with Mesopotamia. The Nile River is associated with Egypt.

questions.question: Mahabharata : India :: Gilgamesh : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (Sumeria). The Mahabharata is an epic from India. The Epic of Gilgamesh is from Sumeria (Mesopotamia).

questions.question: Italy : Latin :: Greece : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (Greek). Latin is the language associated with Italy. Greek is the language associated with Greece.

questions.question: Sistine Madonna : Raphael :: Last Supper : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (Leonardo da Vinci). The Sistine Madonna was painted by Raphael. The Last Supper was painted by Leonardo da Vinci.

questions.question: Stalagmite : Floor :: Stalactite : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (Ceiling). Stalagmites grow upward from the floor. Stalactites hang down from the ceiling.

questions.question: Catholic : Priest :: Moslem : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (Imam). A priest is a religious leader in Catholicism. An imam is a religious leader in Islam.

questions.question: Gionnani Boccaccio : Decameron :: Niccolo Machiavelli : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (The Prince). Boccaccio wrote The Decameron. Machiavelli wrote The Prince.

questions.question: Samuel Morse : Telegraph :: Alexander Graham Bell : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (telephone). Samuel Morse invented the telegraph. Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone.

questions.question: Parachute : Andre Jacques Garnerin :: Television : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (John Logie Baird). Andre Jacques Garnerin invented the parachute. John Logie Baird is credited with inventing the television.

questions.question: Earth is the center : Ptolemy :: Sun is the center : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (Copernicus). Ptolemy proposed the geocentric model (Earth-centered). Copernicus proposed the heliocentric model (Sun-centered).

questions.question: Pythagorean Theorem : Pythagoras :: Cubic Equation : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (Tartaglia). The Pythagorean Theorem is attributed to Pythagoras. The solution to the cubic equation is attributed to Tartaglia.

questions.question: Henry Cavendish : Hydrogen :: Joseph Priestly : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (oxygen). Henry Cavendish discovered hydrogen. Joseph Priestley discovered oxygen.

questions.question: Allied Powers : Russia :: Central Powers : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (Austria). In WWI, Russia was part of the Allied Powers. Austria was part of the Central Powers.

questions.question: entourage : attendants :: cortege : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (procession for a saint). An entourage is a group of attendants. A cortege is a solemn procession, often for a funeral or religious event.

questions.question: islet : small island :: rivulet : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (small river). An islet is a small island. A rivulet is a small river or stream.

questions.question: conspicuous : obvious :: hideous : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (ugly). Conspicuous means obvious. Hideous means ugly.

questions.question: nose : nasal :: abdomen : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (abdominal). 'Nasal' relates to the nose. 'Abdominal' relates to the abdomen.

questions.question: agnostic : doubts God's existence :: atheist : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (denies God's existence). An agnostic doubts or is uncertain about God's existence. An atheist outright denies God's existence.

questions.question: infanticide : killing of infants :: genocide : ?

choices.a: killing of a race or ethnic group

questions.explanation: The analogy is based on definitions. The suffix '-cide' refers to killing. Just as infanticide is the act of killing infants, genocide is the deliberate killing of a large group of people, specifically those of a particular race, nation, or ethnic group.

questions.question: latrine : toilet :: lavatory : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (bathroom). Latrine and toilet are synonyms. Lavatory and bathroom are synonyms.

questions.question: masticate : chew :: eradicate : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (destroy). Masticate means to chew. Eradicate means to destroy completely.

questions.question: sadism : delight in cruelty to others :: masochism : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (delight in being abused). Sadism is deriving pleasure from inflicting pain on others. Masochism is deriving pleasure from receiving pain.

questions.question: mazurka : Polish :: fandango : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (Spanish). The mazurka is a Polish dance. The fandango is a Spanish dance.

questions.question: nearsighted : myopia :: farsighted : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (hyperopia). Myopia is the medical term for nearsightedness. Hyperopia is the medical term for farsightedness.

questions.question: dyslexia : reading :: aphasia : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (speech). Dyslexia is a learning disorder affecting reading. Aphasia is a language disorder affecting speech production or comprehension.

questions.question: maitre d' : head of a restaurant :: busboy : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (waiter's help). A maitre d' is the head of a restaurant. A busboy is an assistant to the waitstaff.

questions.question: figurine : small figure :: heroine : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (female hero). A figurine is a small figure. A heroine is a female hero.

questions.question: Xerox : photocopier :: Adidas : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A (athlete's shoes). Xerox is a brand name for photocopiers. Adidas is a brand name for athletic shoes.

questions.question: Sayonara : Goodbye :: Bonjour : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (Good day). 'Sayonara' is Japanese for 'Goodbye.' 'Bonjour' is French for 'Good day' or 'Hello.'

questions.question: superfluous : excessive :: supersede : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D (take the place of). 'Superfluous' means excessive. 'Supersede' means to take the place of.

questions.question: Nativity : Christmas :: Senakulo : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B (Lent). The Nativity is associated with Christmas. The Senakulo (Passion play) is associated with Lent.

questions.question: theme : main idea :: moral : ?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C (a piece of advice). The theme is the main idea of a story. The moral is a piece of advice or lesson taught by a story.

questions.question: __No one__ __were__ __happy__ __about__ the Mindanao crisis.
questions.explanation: The indefinite pronoun 'No one' is singular and requires a singular verb. The correct verb form is 'was.' The error is in choice B: 'were' should be replaced with 'was' to achieve subject-verb agreement.

questions.question: __The House of Representatives__ __decision__ to decrease the budget for the __Department of Education__ __was met__ with protests.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'The House of Representatives' must be in the possessive form to modify 'decision.' The correct form is 'The House of Representatives' decision' (with an apostrophe after the 's'). Choice A contains the error because it lacks the necessary apostrophe.

questions.question: __The Cabinet__ __regularly__ __meet__ __once__ a week.
questions.explanation: The collective noun 'The Cabinet' is treated as singular in this context. The verb must agree with a singular subject, so 'meet' should be 'meets.' The error is in choice C.

questions.question: __Both__ the Senators and the Congressmen __legislates__ __laws__.
questions.explanation: The compound subject 'the Senators and the Congressmen' is plural. The verb must be the plural form 'legislate,' not the singular 'legislates.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __The Philippine government__ __have__ three branches of powers: the executive, the legislative and the __judicial__.
questions.explanation: The subject 'The Philippine government' is singular. The verb should be 'has,' not 'have.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __The Supreme Court__ __upholds__ the highest principles and standards of morality as embodied in the __Constitution__.
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. The singular subject 'The Supreme Court' agrees with the singular verb 'upholds,' and all other elements are properly constructed.

questions.question: __Some historians__ __contests__ the __origin__ of the __Filipino flag__.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Some historians' is plural, so the verb should be the plural form 'contest' (without the -s). The error is in choice B, which incorrectly uses the singular verb 'contests.'

questions.question: __Some believe__ that the flag we use now is __not the same__ as the one made by __Marcella Agoncillo__.
questions.explanation: The sentence contains no grammatical error. The indefinite pronoun 'Some' correctly takes the plural verb 'believe,' and the rest of the sentence is well-formed.

questions.question: __Either Prof. Teodoro Agoncillo or Dr. Gregorio F. Zaide__ __affirm__ the history of __our flag__.

choices.a: Either Prof. Teodoro Agoncillo or Dr. Gregorio F. Zaide

questions.explanation: With the correlative conjunction 'either...or,' the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Dr. Gregorio F. Zaide' is singular, so the verb should be the singular form 'affirms.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __The news__ __are__ written immediately to meet the previous __deadline__.
questions.explanation: The noun 'news' is singular in form and meaning, even though it ends in -s. It requires the singular verb 'is' instead of 'are.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __Attempts__ __is made__ to __locate__ and restore the last original Filipino flag.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Attempts' is plural, so the verb should be the plural form 'are made.' The error is in choice B, which incorrectly uses the singular verb 'is made.'

questions.question: __Both Chelle and Charm__ __enjoys__ __reading__.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Both Chelle and Charm' forms a plural subject. The verb must be the plural form 'enjoy' rather than the singular 'enjoys.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __Reading books__ __widens__ one's __horizons__.
questions.explanation: The subject is the gerund phrase 'Reading books,' which functions as a singular noun. The singular verb 'widens' correctly agrees with it. The sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.question: __If everybody__ __know__ how to read, __then books will__ never cease to be useful.
questions.explanation: The indefinite pronoun 'everybody' is singular and requires the singular verb 'knows.' The error is in choice B, where the plural form 'know' is used.

questions.question: __No one__ __dares__ to question how __invaluable__ books are.
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. The singular subject 'No one' agrees with the singular verb 'dares,' and 'invaluable' is the correct word choice.

questions.question: __Great literary works__ __enriches__ the __vocabulary__ of their readers.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Great literary works' is plural, so the verb should be the plural form 'enrich.' The error is in choice B, which uses the singular verb 'enriches.'

questions.question: __Have either__ of the __books__ __been returned__?
questions.explanation: The indefinite pronoun 'either' is singular, so the auxiliary verb should be 'Has,' not 'Have.' The correct phrasing is 'Has either of the books been returned?' The error is in choice A.

questions.question: __One hundred fifty pesos__ __are__ the average __selling price__ of one textbook.
questions.explanation: When a sum of money is treated as a single amount, it takes a singular verb. 'One hundred fifty pesos' is singular in this context, so the verb should be 'is,' not 'are.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __One of the machines in the printing press__ __weren't__ __working__.

choices.a: One of the machines in the printing press

questions.explanation: The subject is 'One,' which is singular. The verb must agree, so the correct form is 'wasn't' instead of the plural 'weren't.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __Either the teachers or the librarian__ __take care__ __of the books__.

choices.a: Either the teachers or the librarian

questions.explanation: In an 'either...or' construction, the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. 'The librarian' is singular, so the verb should be the singular form 'takes care.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __A number of books__ __is regularly__ donated __to public schools__.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'A number of' is an idiomatic expression meaning 'several' and takes a plural verb. The verb should be 'are' instead of 'is.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __The number of readers__ __continually rise__ __each year__.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'The number' is singular and requires a singular verb. The verb should be 'rises,' not the plural 'rise.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __For I__, Reader's Digest is __informative__ as well as __entertaining__.
questions.explanation: The pronoun is the object of the preposition 'for' and must be in the objective case. 'For I' should be 'For me.' The error is in choice A.

questions.question: __The Manila Bulletin__ __has been published__ the Panorama magazine __for over__ a hundred years.
questions.explanation: The intended meaning is that The Manila Bulletin is the publisher, so the active voice is needed. The correct phrase is 'has been publishing,' not the passive 'has been published.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __All children__ __has__ inherent rights __that must be protected__.
questions.explanation: The subject 'All children' is plural. The verb must be the plural form 'have,' not the singular 'has.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __The editor-in-chief, together with the writers,__ __confers__ __about the contents__ of their newspaper.

choices.a: The editor-in-chief, together with the writers

questions.explanation: The subject is 'The editor-in-chief,' which is singular. The phrase 'together with the writers' is a prepositional modifier and does not make the subject plural. The singular verb 'confers' agrees correctly. The sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.question: __Gorio and Tecla, in addition to Captain Barbel,__ __was__ a popular __comic book__ during the '70s.

choices.a: Gorio and Tecla, in addition to Captain Barbel

questions.explanation: The compound subject 'Gorio and Tecla' is plural. The phrase 'in addition to Captain Barbel' does not affect the number of the subject. The verb should be the plural form 'were.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __Pol Medina__ __has drew__ the very famous __Pugad Baboy__ characters.
questions.explanation: The present perfect tense requires the past participle. The past participle of 'draw' is 'drawn,' not 'drew.' The correct form is 'has drawn.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __Pugad Baboy__ __first appear__ in the __Philippine Daily__ Inquirer during the late '80s.
questions.explanation: The sentence refers to a past event ('during the late '80s'), so the past tense is required. The verb should be 'first appeared,' not the base form 'appear.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __Neither Pol Medina nor his friends__ __thinks__ he __will become__ successful.

choices.a: Neither Pol Medina nor his friends

questions.explanation: With the correlative conjunction 'neither...nor,' the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'His friends' is plural, so the verb should be the plural form 'think,' not the singular 'thinks.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __Some believes__ that Mr. Medina's works __satirize__ the __socio-economic__ condition of the people in our country.
questions.explanation: The pronoun 'Some' refers to people and is plural. The verb should be the plural form 'believe,' not 'believes.' The error is in choice A.

questions.question: __The youth delegates__ __have been sang__ __the National Anthem__.
questions.explanation: The verb form 'sang' is the simple past of 'sing,' not the past participle. After 'have been,' the past participle is required. The correct form is 'have been sung' (passive) or 'have been singing' (progressive). The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __That house and lot in the corner__ __are__ __government-owned__.

choices.a: That house and lot in the corner

questions.explanation: The phrase 'That house and lot' refers to a single property considered as one unit. It takes a singular verb, so 'are' should be replaced with 'is.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __The number of socialized housing units sponsored by the government__ __increases__ __each year__.

choices.a: The number of socialized housing units sponsored by the government

questions.explanation: The subject is 'The number,' which is singular. The singular verb 'increases' correctly agrees with it. The sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.question: __A quarter of the government tax collections__ __goes__ to __infrastructure__ projects.

choices.a: A quarter of the government tax collections

questions.explanation: When a fraction like 'a quarter of' precedes a plural noun, the verb can be singular if the fraction is thought of as a unit. Here, 'goes' is acceptable, and the sentence contains no grammatical error.

questions.question: __The beneficiaries__ of the study grant given by the government__ __will be__ __them__.
questions.explanation: The pronoun follows the linking verb 'will be' and serves as a predicate nominative. It must be in the subjective case: 'they,' not the objective 'them.' The error is in choice C.

questions.question: __Studies suggests__ that __exposure to__ too much violence on television __makes__ one equally violent.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Studies' is plural, so the verb should be the plural form 'suggest,' not 'suggests.' The error is in choice A.

questions.question: __The possible effects of television viewing__ __needs__ __to be explored__ further.

choices.a: The possible effects of television viewing

questions.explanation: The subject is 'effects,' which is plural. The verb should be the plural form 'need,' not the singular 'needs.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __Every weekdays__, Chel and Charm __goes__ to school __together__.
questions.explanation: The determiner 'every' is followed by a singular noun. The correct phrase is 'Every weekday,' not the plural 'weekdays.' The error is in choice A. (Note: the verb 'goes' is also incorrect for the compound subject, but the designated answer points to the determiner-noun agreement error.)

questions.question: __The Scent of Apples__, a story about a Filipino who __immigrated__ to the United States, __are written__ by Bienvenido Santos.
questions.explanation: The title of a single work, 'The Scent of Apples,' is singular. The verb must be the singular form 'is written,' not 'are written.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: Nick Joaquin, one of the exceptional Filipino __writers, is__ also __known__ __for__ Quijano de Manila.
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. The singular verb 'is' agrees with the singular subject 'Nick Joaquin,' and the appositive 'one of the exceptional Filipino writers' does not change the subject-verb agreement. 'Known for' is idiomatic and acceptable.

questions.question: __Some people believes__ that one __could see__ his future mate by __looking into__ a mirror on May day eve.
questions.explanation: The noun 'people' is plural. The verb should be the plural form 'believe,' not the singular 'believes.' The error is in choice A.

questions.question: __Jose Garcia Villa__ was a recipient of numerous awards. __between them__, the __"National Artist Award for Literature"__.
questions.explanation: The preposition 'between' is used for two entities. Since 'numerous awards' refers to more than two, 'among' should be used. The error is in choice B: 'between them' should be 'among them.'

questions.question: __The Far Eastern University (FEU) also gave he__ a __Doctor of Literature__ __honoris causa__ in 1959, aside from asking him to be a visiting professor.

choices.a: The Far Eastern University (FEU) also gave he

questions.explanation: The indirect object of the verb 'gave' must be in the objective case. The correct pronoun is 'him,' not the subjective 'he.' The error is in choice A.

questions.question: __Between the numerous prose writers__, I __think__ Nick Joaquin is __the best__.
questions.explanation: The preposition 'Between' is used for two items; for more than two, 'Among' is required. Since there are 'numerous prose writers,' 'Between' should be replaced with 'Among.' The error is in choice A.

questions.question: __Those__ __are work__ of __famous authors__.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Those' is plural, so the complement should also be plural. 'Work' should be the plural form 'works' to agree. The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __The professor__ asked her a question __about__ __they__.
questions.explanation: The pronoun follows the preposition 'about' and must be in the objective case. The correct form is 'them,' not the subjective 'they.' The error is in choice C.

questions.question: __Literature__ __seem__ elusive to people __who profess__ indifference to it.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Literature' is singular. The verb must agree and should be the singular form 'seems,' not 'seem.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __It appeals both__ to the __readers intellect__ __and passion__.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'readers intellect' requires a possessive form. It should be 'reader's intellect' (singular possessive) or 'readers' intellects' (plural possessive). The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __Robert Frost, an American poet,__ __defines__ literature as __"performance in words"__.
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. The appositive 'an American poet' correctly modifies the subject, and the singular verb 'defines' agrees with the singular subject.

questions.question: __Either of the authors__ __have received__ citations for __their remarkable works__.
questions.explanation: The indefinite pronoun 'Either' is singular and requires a singular auxiliary verb. 'Have received' should be 'has received.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __Just like Edgar Allan Poe__, it is believed that Nick Joaquin __starts getting__ ideas after he __has drank__ alcoholic beverages.
questions.explanation: The past participle of 'drink' is 'drunk,' not 'drank.' The present perfect form should be 'has drunk.' The error is in choice C.

questions.question: __Computers__ __are widely use__ nowadays even in __preschools__.
questions.explanation: The passive voice requires the past participle. The correct form is 'are widely used,' not the base form 'use.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __The number__ of Computer Science __students__ __steadily increases__.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'The number' is singular and takes the singular verb 'increases.' The sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.question: __AMA, in addition to STI,__ __train__ students to be __proficient__ in computer use.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular noun 'AMA.' The prepositional phrase 'in addition to STI' does not make the subject plural. The verb should be the singular form 'trains,' not 'train.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __Knowledge__ __should__ always __be put__ to good use.
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. The modal verb 'should' is followed by the base form, and 'be put' correctly forms the passive infinitive. There is no error.

questions.question: __One of the viruses__ __has infect__ my brother's __brand new__ laptop computer.
questions.explanation: The present perfect tense requires the past participle. The correct form is 'has infected,' not the base form 'infect.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __Internet access__ __allow__ us __to communicate__ with other people anywhere in the world.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Internet access' is singular. The verb must be the singular form 'allows,' not 'allow.' The error is in choice B.

questions.question: __All of the pens__ __are spent__ __yesterday__.
questions.explanation: The time expression 'yesterday' indicates past tense. The verb should be the past form 'were spent,' not the present 'are spent.' The error is in choice B.

B. Otherwise, the bill will go back to the House from where it originated, and it will be deliberated upon again. — gives the alternative outcome if the bill is not approved

Therefore, the correct answer is D.

passageGroups.title: Epicureanism
passageGroups.passage:
The concepts of Epicureanism are largely known to us through Lucretius, rather than Epicurus. The latter, born an Athenian citizen in Samos in 341, founded his school in his garden, a symbol of retirement from the world, in 306 and died in 270 B.C.

For the Epicurean, the universe was chaotic and anarchic, composed of atoms and the void. All knowledge was acquired by sense perception; observation was therefore essential to understanding. There were an infinite number of worlds, formed by the chance combination of atoms in infinite space. The gods, unconcerned about human affairs, lived in the void between the different worlds. They were not to be regarded superstitiously or feared, only to be envied.

Man himself was made up of body and soul. Death was not to be feared. There was no such thing as immortality; after death, atoms of the soul were scattered. The aim of life therefore was pleasure, the pursuit of which brought about happiness, the final end. The injunction to follow nature meant, seek pleasure. Everything was desirable insofar as it led to pleasure, but above all, the aim was absence of pain and the achievement of peace of mind. This would be obtained personally by self-control, the mastery and limitation of desires as far as possible to those that were strictly necessary. Also, it implied limitation of social relationships — 'live unknown' — refusal to be involved in family or political affairs, skepticism toward religion, which the Epicureans considered largely superstition.

From: The Great Political Theories, Vol.1 by Michael Curtis

passageGroups.passage:
One day, the guru and his young disciples were seated on the bank of the river, talking and praying together. An uprooted tree came floating down the river and caught in the bank just in front of them. Caught in the branches of the tree was a scorpion which must have been trapped on the tree when it was uprooted by the floodwater upstream. The guru knew that, inevitably, the scorpion would fall from the tree and be drowned in the river. So he reached his hand out to take the scorpion from the tree and to put it safely on land. But as he reached out to rescue the scorpion, it stung his hand, and the guru had to take his hand away in pain.

After a moment, the guru reached out to rescue the scorpion again, and the scorpion stung him again. The guru kept trying to save the scorpion and the scorpion kept stinging him until his hand was red and swollen in pain.

Finally, one of the young disciples could control himself no longer and he burst out: 'Master, why do you keep trying to rescue that foolish scorpion that doesn't even want to be saved?' The guru looked very patiently at the impetuous young disciple and said: 'Should I be untrue to my nature which is to be compassionate just because this scorpion is being true to its nature to sting?'

Henri Nouwen

passageGroups.title: Cancer
passageGroups.passage:
Cancer is a disease in which cells somehow become activated into uncontrolled multiplication and thus produce an overgrowth, or tumor, composed of malformed, malignant cells. Cancerous tumors can occur in almost any tissue of the body, although some are more often affected than others. Three general kinds of cancer, named after the tissues most often affected, are recognized: carcinomas (from karkinoma, the Greek word for cancer), which commonly involve epithelial tissue (epidermis and lining membranes); sarcomas (Greek sarkoma, 'flesh'), which affect mainly connective tissues, including bone; and leukemias, which start in the bone marrow and lymphatic tissues and spread in the blood and lymph.

passageGroups.title: Blood Clot Formation
passageGroups.passage:
When the tissues of the body are wounded, several events occur that resist the loss of blood from the cut vessels and begin the healing processes. At the wound site, blood platelets swell and burst, releasing chemicals that cause the arteries to constrict and thus slow the loss of blood. The platelets also initiate a process that results in activation of prothrombin activator, an enzyme that converts a blood-protein constituent called prothrombin to thrombin. In the presence of calcium ions, thrombin catalyzes the conversion of another blood-protein component, fibrinogen, into fibrin threads. The fibrin threads form a fine meshwork in the blood and together with trapped cells and other blood particles make a clot and block further the escape of blood from the wound. In the hereditary disease hemophilia, the blood fails to clot, and the victim bleeds to death even from a small wound.

From: Biology by Norstog and Meyernecks
